scope.summary: Implement pose authority and the pose library per Section 13.18 (BK-18.3, TAI-BK-064), closing AREQ-003: BodyPoseAsset (BPA-) stores per-bone transforms PLUS the morph context (authored_channels snapshot and active pins); applying a pose to a body with different channel values re-solves in morph context via IK retarget over the target body's proportions — never a raw transform copy. Saves emit TailorBodyPoseAssetSaved; applications emit TailorBodyPoseApplied.
acceptance_criteria: BodyPoseAsset matches the TAI-BK-064 shape: pose_asset_id "BPA-{uuid_v7}", name, skeleton_version, bone_transforms (BTreeMap<String, PoseBoneTransform>, mm/quaternions), authored_channels snapshot, pins (Vec<IkPin>); persisted via guarded storage with ledger events.

apply_pose(body_id, pose_asset_id) re-solves when the target body's channel map differs from authored_channels: pinned contact bones are used as IK re-solve anchors over the target proportions; a raw-copy code path for mismatched contexts does not exist (negative test).

Retarget proof: a pose authored on the neutral body applied to a petite + breast_volume 3.0 body keeps feet on the ground plane and hands within tolerance of their authored relative targets (proportion-adjusted assertions).
Skeleton version mismatch between pose and body is a typed rejection (TAI-BK-058 compatibility law).
TailorBodyPoseAssetSaved and TailorBodyPoseApplied are registered in the tailor.body family and emitted with pose/body ids; replaying the events reproduces the final pose state (TAI-BK-072).
Consumes hsk.tailor.body_pose_contact_set@1 from MT-714 as the sole pin/contact authority and does not introduce a parallel contact record.
Registers hsk.tailor.body_pose_asset@1 as the canonical immutable BodyPoseAsset schema with pose revision and sha256:<64hex> semantic content hash produced from crate::llm::canonical_json_bytes_nfc.

The BodyPose hash includes schema/version/revision, typed body and pose ids, skeleton/rest-pose hash, body-channel snapshot hash, bone transforms with units/frame conventions, canonical hsk.tailor.body_pose_contact_set@1 hash, and source/proposal lineage; it excludes only storage-local surrogate ids, timestamps, and receipts.

Unknown major versions fail closed and accepted older versions require an explicit deterministic migration; save, apply, list, get, replay, and link-back always verify the immutable payload hash before use.
scope.risk_if_missed: Raw-copied pose transforms are why Daz pose products break on non-default bodies (feet floating, hands interpenetrating); without morph-context re-solve, the pose library is useless across the operator's wildly varied archetypes — which is the entire production population.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit skeleton and rigging

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT emits typed diagnostics through its owning command or job and inherits retention, health, and projection behavior from the shared diagnostics substrate.
The owning native shell or scheduled job supplies Palmistry coverage; this MT must preserve operation identity and recovery handles.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.

requirements: Resolve Principal, AuthenticatedSession and AccessSpace before every resource read or mutation.
Use PostgreSQL RLS/FORCE RLS and ResourceBroker-backed artifact/file handles; UI filtering is never the security boundary.
Derived resources preserve the intersection of source access scopes and must not leak existence through counts, search, previews, logs, traces, caches, diagnostics, exports or model context.
